bench.drop.what: take a served node's port back, or with no node named cut every attached client loose while leaving the listeners open

params.name: node
params.what: the node to stop serving, whether or not a client is on it; absent drops the clients instead and stops serving nothing

bench.drop.answers: `dropped` counts what was closed, and zero is a normal answer: named a node nothing was serving, or asked to drop clients when none were attached.

bench.refresh.what: look again at which endpoints are open and which have a client on them, because a client attaching or leaving tells this session nothing
bench.refresh.answers: It answers with nothing at all. The endpoints go into the published state, which is where a panel reads them.

example.what: see whether a client has attached

bench.serve.what: open a real endpoint onto one simulated node, so an unmodified companion client on this machine or another can talk to it as if it were hardware

params.name: node
params.what: the node to serve; absent takes the first companion in the scenario, because an endpoint is what is wanted before a node has been chosen

params.name: kind
params.what: "serial" for a pseudo-terminal a serial client opens; anything else, absent included, listens on TCP on every interface and a port the operating system picks the first time this node is served

bench.serve.answers: Serving takes the port off the workbench, so a companion session on that node is released rather than shared. A second call for the same node replaces the listener rather than adding one, and keeps the address: the port is drawn once per node and asked for again on every serve after, including after a drop, because a client already pointed at the first address cannot be told about a second. A port taken by something else in the meantime moves the endpoint and says so.

example.what: put a node on a TCP port for a real client

bench.stray.what: hand a companion a frame it was never going to be sent, so what the decoder does with rubbish can be watched rather than assumed
bench.stray.answers: It injects at the first companion in the scenario, and names which that was. Refused where there is no run, or where the scenario holds no companion at all.

example.what: put a bad frame at a companion
